author: barnabemonnot
content: Very cool result indeed! I haven't dug into the details yet, for latency reduction, it's less RTP that matters since we can always shrink the per block gas limit to maintain throughput while partitioning the work in smaller chunks, but the latency of recursion, which is a cost paid for each chunk of work (and so shorter slots => more chunks => more fixed overhead => less room to scale down per block gas limit while maintaining throughput).

author: barnabemonnot
content:
on this, yes it's a similar reasoning to the gas limit: independently from a slot time reduction, we may want to increase the blob throughput. it's possible (though maybe unlikely?) that the throughput increase we want is 20% given a slot time decrease of 16.6%. if it is, then we don't need to change the blob schedule.

as a note, ethlabs / <@421767904053297152> is working on a survey to uncover the blob capacity that is demanded but not currently supplied. we should have clearer expectations after this
